raw_text:
Write concise, idiomatic C# for this .NET 10/C# 14 codebase. Prefer simplicity; keep changes focused and minimal. **Avoid over-engineering—don't add features, abstractions, or "improvements" beyond what's requested.**

Structure: `Commands/` CLI, `Configuration/` TOML, `Download/` orchestration, `Http/` Transmission controllers, `Services/` API clients, `Program.cs` entry/DI; tests in `tests/Csharparr.Tests/` (`Configuration/`, `Download/`, `Http/`, `Services/`, `Integration/`).

Conventions: PascalCase types/methods/public members; camelCase locals/parameters; `_camelCase` private fields; sparing UPPER_CASE constants; `I` interfaces. Use file-scoped namespaces, records for DTOs/immutable data, pattern matching, nullable reference types, top-level `Program.cs`, `[]` for empty collections, `Lock` (not `object`), primary constructors when suitable, raw strings when useful. Use `var` when obvious; explicit types for clarity; expression bodies for simple members; `?.`, `??`, `??=`, interpolation; methods focused and under ~50 lines when possible.

All I/O must be async; always pass `CancellationToken` through calls; optional token parameters use `cancellationToken = default`; async methods end in `Async`. Catch `OperationCanceledException` separately; log expected cancellation at Debug, not Error. Use `BackgroundService` for long-running tasks; `Channel<T>` with bounded queues for producer-consumer work; track background tasks, periodically clean completed tasks.

HTTP: typed clients (`AddHttpClient<IPutioClient, PutioClient>`), named clients (`AddHttpClient("ArrClient")`) for shared configuration, per-client/operation timeouts, and `IHttpClientFactory` in background services. Use `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` (not deprecated `Polly.Extensions.Http`); exponential backoff with jitter, circuit breakers, appropriate timeouts. Retry network errors (`HttpRequestException`), timeouts (`TimeoutException`, `TaskCanceledException`), and transient statuses 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504.

DI: register config as singleton; services through interfaces; typed HTTP clients with interfaces; factories for dynamic clients. Always register services with their interfaces, not concrete types. Test DI resolution and concurrent resolution.

Use exceptions for exceptional cases, not control flow; domain exceptions (`PutioException`, `ArrClientException`). Include HTTP error response body in messages, truncated to 500 chars. Log `BrokenCircuitException` at Debug; socket errors at Warning without full stack trace. Continue processing other operations when one service fails.

Use structured logging, not interpolation. Levels: Debug operational detail; Information important events; Warning recovered/expected failures; Error failures needing attention; Fatal application-ending failures. Reduce framework noise; `Microsoft.Hosting.Lifetime: Information`. Use thread-safe collections or locks for shared state; periodically clean resources and expired entries.

Tests: xUnit, Moq, FluentAssertions, `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing`. Test happy/error paths; mock HTTP/external dependencies; integration-test DI. Always verify new controllers and services resolve from DI (see `tests/Integration/`). Use FluentAssertions.

Use Tomlyn; validate config at startup with detailed errors, reporting all errors at once. Config: `username`, `password` HTTP basic auth; `instance_name` 3–10 alphanumeric characters; `instance_folder_id` Put.io folder ID; `download_directory` local path; `putio.api_key` token; at least one arr service.

Implement Transmission RPC for *arr compatibility; `[Route("/transmission/rpc")]`; preserve JSON property names (`PropertyNamingPolicy = null`). Provide `/health` returning simple 200 OK. Use multi-stage Dockerfile, non-root user, HEALTHCHECK. Platforms: linux-x64, linux-arm64, osx-x64, osx-arm64.

Don't add features or refactor beyond what's requested
Don't add comments, docstrings, or type annotations to unchanged code
Don't create helpers or abstractions for one-time operations
Don't add error handling for scenarios that can't happen
Don't use `Polly.Extensions.Http` (deprecated)—use `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience`
Don't log at Error level for expected conditions (cancellation, circuit breaker)
Don't use string interpolation in log messages
Don't register concrete types when interfaces exist
